US financial-sector outperformance (HOOD, FUJI) is creating a sentiment halo for Indonesian brokers and payment processors, but local liquidity remains the binding constraint for sustained upside.

Add selectively to large-cap banks (BBNI, BMRI) for dividend yield and rate-cycle tailwinds; avoid chasing small-cap fintech spikes without earnings confirmation.

US infrastructure and energy-transition spending continues to lift global metals demand, benefiting IDX-listed miners with US revenue exposure.

sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: Indonesia's renewable energy mandate and JETP funding commitments create a durable pipeline for solar, geothermal, and battery storage developers, favoring local champions like TOBA and TPIA.
Downstream climate-tech segments—waste-to-energy, EV charging, and green hydrogen—are gaining traction as provincial governments enforce emissions targets, benefiting LAPD and PKPK.
US renewable policy uncertainty and high interest rates cap upside for US-listed names like PLUG, reinforcing a home-market bias for Indonesia-focused investors.
sectors.ai: Buy selective Indonesian renewables names on domestic strength despite US drag; TOBA and TPIA lead with structural policy tailwinds. Rotate into LAPD and PKPK for downstream exposure. Avoid US-listed PLUG until margin visibility improves. Position for Q3 earnings catalysts and JETP-linked project awards.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG

Structural shift toward food-away-from-home (NASI, CARS) and tech-enabled retail (NANO, BTEK) is accelerating, supported by rising urban middle-class spending and digital adoption.
sectors.ai: Buy selective small-cap FMCG names showing volume-driven re-rating (AGAR, BTEK, NAYZ) while large caps lag; US strength (+1.00%) supports export-linked consumer plays. Rotate into food-service and specialty retail sub-sectors with earnings momentum, avoid broad index exposure. Target 3-6 week horizon, set tight stops at 5% below entry given normal signal volatility.

Prioritize large-cap US names (HCA, ZTS, BMY) over local healthcare, as US momentum and pipeline catalysts will outperform Indonesian regulatory overhangs in the next quarter.
